items.output:
Snow fell steadily through Friday afternoon, piling against the cabin windows until the garden disappeared. I stoked the stove and listened to the timber settle as the temperature dropped below freezing. Evening came quick and complete; the only light was the fire and the pale blue dusk beyond the glass.

Saturday stayed under a blanket of white. I read by the window, tea going cold, watching a jackerel pick its way through the pines. No signals, no schedule, just the slow turning of the day.

Sunday brought a clear, brittle morning. The sky went a hard blue and the snow cracked underfoot. I walked the frozen trail around the lake, breath pluming, before returning to the warmth of the cabin and the last embers in the stove.

More soon.

# Learning to Swim as an Adult

The water looked deeper than it was. I stood at the edge with my heart pounding. Every adult learner carries the same fear of looking foolish. I dropped into the pool on a Tuesday morning. The coach counted to three and I let go. My legs flailed at first. Then I found a rhythm. Breathing became the hardest part. I turned my head to inhale and swallowed a mouthful. Practice turned panic into patience. Each week my strokes grew longer. Now I glide across the lane with ease. The pool forgives every mistake.

More soon.
